accepted.question_text: Can one give an elementary proof of the Hirzebruch signature theorem for closed smooth oriented manifolds, namely the theorem identifying the signature tau(M) with the L-polynomial in the Pontryagin classes evaluated on the fundamental class, and can one explain geometrically the functional equation for the associated virtual signature?
accepted.context_brief: Elementary proof of the signature theorem

evidence.quote: Problem 3 (Hirzebruch-Thom). Give an elementary proof of the index theorem and explain the geometrical meaning of the functional equation valid for tau.
To this day no proof of the signature theorem is known that would qualify as "elementary", and so Problem 3 is wide open.

accepted.question_text: For a given closed subgroup H of GL(n, R), is there a general criterion that decides whether an n-manifold admits an integrable H-structure, rather than only case-by-case criteria for special geometric structures such as almost complex, symplectic, or foliation-type structures?

evidence.quote: Problem 9, attributed to E. Calabi, asks for a general criterion to determine whether a manifold Mn admits an integrable H-structure, for some given closed subgroup H subset GL(n, R).

As explained in [Hi87], many important cases of this problem have been resolved, but the methods and techniques used are very different in the different cases, suggesting that the general formulation attempted by Calabi may in fact not be appropriate.

accepted.question_text: Given an integer r with 0 <= r <= k, what criterion determines whether a manifold of dimension 2k+1 admits a globally defined Pfaffian equation whose class is everywhere exactly 2r+1, equivalently a 1-form alpha such that alpha wedge (d alpha)^r is nowhere zero while alpha wedge (d alpha)^(r+1) vanishes identically?

evidence.quote: Open problems. I believe that the following problems are essentially open: ... Problem 10 (existence of Pfaffians of constant class).

Problem 10 (Chern). A Pfaffian equation in M2k+1 can be locally reduced to the normal form ... The number r being fixed, give a criterion to determine whether M2k+1 admits a Pfaffian equation in the large whose class is 2r + 1 everywhere.

accepted.question_text: For each n, what is the minimal Euclidean dimension into which real projective n-space RP^n can be smoothly embedded? In particular, for RP^6, is the minimal embedding dimension 10 rather than the currently known upper bound 11 and the ruled-out value 8?
accepted.context_brief: Optimal embeddings of real projective spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 11 (Chern). Let n + d(n) be the minimum dimension of an Euclidean space in which the n-dimensional real projective space Pn can be differentiably imbedded.

However, the more general question implicit in Chern's problem, namely to determine for every n the optimal embedding dimension for Pn, is still open. For example, it is now known that P6 embeds in R11, but it is unknown whether it embeds in R10.

accepted.question_text: Does four-dimensional Euclidean space E^4 contain a closed surface of genus 2 whose induced metric has Gaussian curvature negative at every point, and can such an example even be chosen to have constant negative Gaussian curvature?
accepted.context_brief: Negatively curved genus-2 surfaces in E^4

evidence.quote: Problem 12 (Chern). A closed surface M in the 4-dimensional Euclidean space E4 has an induced Riemannian metric and hence a Gaussian curvature K. Does there exist such a surface for which K < 0 everywhere? In particular, does there exist a surface of genus 2 in E4 for which K < 0 everywhere?
It is still an open question whether one can reduce the genus to 2, and whether one can make the curvature constant.

accepted.question_text: For an almost-complex manifold M, are the dimensions h^{p,q} defined as the kernel dimensions of the d-bar Laplacian independent of the choice of Hermitian metric, and if not, is there a replacement notion of h^{p,q} depending only on the almost-complex structure that extends Dolbeault cohomology from the integrable case?
accepted.context_brief: Dolbeault-type invariants for almost complex manifolds

evidence.quote: Problem 20 (Kodaira-Spencer). Let Mn be an almost-complex manifold. Choose an Hermitian structure and consider the numbers h^{p,q} defined as above. Is h^{p,q} independent of the choice of the Hermitian structure? If not, give some other definition of the h^{p,q} of Mn which depends only on the almost-complex structure and which generalizes the h^{p,q} of a complex manifold.
There seems to have been no progress at all on this problem, which asks for a development of harmonic Dolbeault theory on arbitrary almost complex manifolds.

accepted.question_text: Does complex projective 3-space CP^3 admit a complex structure whose second Chern class vanishes, equivalently a non-Kahler complex structure whose existence would in particular have consequences for the long-standing question of whether S^6 admits a complex structure?
accepted.context_brief: Complex structures on CP^3 with c2 = 0

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Does there exist a complex structure on P3 with vanishing second Chern class?
This problem is still considered to be wide open, although solutions have been claimed repeatedly over the years.

accepted.question_text: For each n >= 3, determine all complex structures on the smooth manifold underlying complex projective space CP^n, including the possible existence and classification of non-Kahler complex structures beyond the standard algebraic one.

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Consider the complex projective space Pn as a differentiable manifold with the usual differentiable structure. Determine all complex structures of Pn.
Both Problem 13 and Problem 28 are open for non-Kahlerian complex structures as soon as n >= 3.

accepted.question_text: If one ranges over all smooth 4-manifolds homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2, rather than fixing the standard smooth manifold itself, must every complex structure on such a manifold come from an even Hirzebruch surface, or can there exist other complex surfaces homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2?
accepted.context_brief: Complex structures on manifolds homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Determine all complex structures of S2 x S2.
If we allow all manifolds homeomorphic to S2 x S2, then the answer is still not known, and in this sense the problem is still open.

accepted.question_text: Which rational linear combinations of Hodge numbers and Chern characteristic numbers of a smooth complex projective variety are topological invariants, under oriented or unoriented homeomorphism or diffeomorphism, and which are not?
accepted.context_brief: Topological invariance of Hodge and Chern data

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Are the h^{p,q} and the Chern characteristic numbers of an algebraic variety Vn topological invariants of Vn? If not, determine all those linear combinations of the h^{p,q} and the Chern characteristic numbers which are topological invariants.

Progress and solutions. I believe the only problem from [Hi54] that was wide open in 1987 and has since been solved completely, is Problem 31, about the topological (non-)invariance of characteristic numbers of algebraic varieties, whose solution is described at the end of this report.
